answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is released only after its work is verified by independent peers. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, reputation accrues slowly from completed, attested jobs, while a reef of shared trust records lets verifiers cross-check claims cheaply. A fake identity must therefore pay the full stake and wait through the same slow build for every copy, and any fraud forfeits the stake and broadcasts a negative signal that poisons all its clones at once, so cloning stops paying.
